A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations on Superconductivity and MNIST, including conditional-expectation errors, classification results, and compressed-set visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds an inverse multi-quadratic kernel ablation and measured runtime results in Appendix C.1.2.

M1.justification: The JKH, JKIP, ACKH, and ACKIP objectives and procedures remain unchanged, as do all eight appendix algorithms. The gradient-flow attribution and compressed-set notation changes do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: The true Gaussian conditional example, Superconductivity, Heteroscedastic, Imbalanced, MNIST, and AMCMD-flexibility examples are retained. The new kernel ablation uses the existing Heteroscedastic data and task.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain JKH, JKIP, ACKH, ACKIP, random sampling, and full-data references where applicable. Expanded discussion of gradient flow, Support Points, and Kernel Thinning does not add evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1.2 adds an evaluation replacing Gaussian kernels with inverse multi-quadratic kernels and a wall-clock-time evaluation across compressed-set sizes. The retained experiments keep their documented splits, sample sizes, metrics, and optimization settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds a kernel-choice ablation testing whether the Heteroscedastic findings persist with inverse multi-quadratic kernels, plus runtime-scaling measurements in Figure 22 and Table 1. Existing case studies and AMCMD-flexibility analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new timing table reports means and standard deviations over twenty runs. Existing performance experiments retain medians, 25th–75th percentiles, and IQR reporting, with twenty method runs and 500 random-sampling runs; no increase in those run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Existing performance curves and boxplots are retained. New IMQ results favor ACKIP across several test functions. Table 1 newly reports mean runtimes of 9.47 seconds for JKH, 0.84 for JKIP, 318.81 for ACKH, and 11.42 for ACKIP; these are additional measurements, not improvements over v2 timings.

T1.justification: Section D.2.5 relaxes the dimensional hierarchy from n >> m >> d,p to n >> d,p and revises the stated dimension factor from 'd or p' to 'd+p'. The central AMCMD definitions, theorems, proofs, and exact Gaussian derivations are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the AMCMD metric, linear-time conditional compression through ACKH/ACKIP, and the same empirical advantages of ACKIP and joint optimization. v3 makes JKIP's gradient-flow ancestry explicit without changing its retained contribution as a joint-distribution compression method.

C2.justification: v3 adds a conditional-density-estimation analogy and a differential-privacy research direction. Section 6 largely relocates v2's applicability and limitations discussion, but omits the explicit acknowledgment that gradient-free variants were not evaluated and the broader suggestion of using JKIP samples for parametric models.

D1.justification: The new checklist supplies a code repository address and states that experiment scripts and a plotting notebook accompany the work; Appendix C.1.2 adds measured runtimes. Existing hardware, software, and hyperparameter disclosures remain. The PDFs alone cannot establish the repository's usability.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1.1–A.1.2 substantially expands positioning relative to standard distribution compression and dataset distillation, including gradient flow, Support Points, and energy distance. JKIP is explicitly connected to Wasserstein gradient flow, and additional literature supports conditional-density motivation and privacy-related future work.

P1.justification: v3 edits the introduction and methodological explanations, adds a main-text related-work paragraph, moves applicability and limitations into Section 6, introduces appendix subheadings, and adds the NeurIPS checklist. Most existing technical prose and the central method–experiment–proof organization remain.

P2.justification: Figures 2, 4, and 6 gain compressed-set-size axis labels while retaining their curves. v3 adds Figures 20–22 and Tables 1–2, expands several captions, and rearranges figures and algorithm displays. Table 2 summarizes previously documented complexity orders.

improvement.justification: The kernel ablation and measured runtimes strengthen robustness and efficiency evidence, while expanded research positioning and clearer plot labels improve interpretation. These focused gains leave the core methods and existing results intact. They outweigh the limited loss of transparency from omitting the explicit statement that gradient-free variants were untested.
